stem: Which trend contributed to the attempt to pass the Equal Rights Amendment in the 1970s?

options.label: A
options.text: Women took on important roles in the investigation into the Watergate scandal.

options.label: B
options.text: Women organized protests against various forms of discrimination.

options.label: C
options.text: Women led the fight to combat propaganda during the Cold War.

options.label: D
options.text: Women accepted senior management positions in large corporations.

visual_elements: The purpose of the ERA [Equal Rights Amendment] was to establish legal gender equality. . . .

In 1970, after decades of receiving little attention . . . the amendment was given serious consideration. By March 1972 the ERA . . . was sent to the states for ratification. Twenty-two states quickly ratified the amendment in 1972. But when the final deadline for ratification arrived . . . it was three states short.
—Christine Blackerby, "The Equal Rights Amendment: The Most Popular Never-Ratified Amendment," National Archives
